2027-06-11.title: Friday of the third week after Pentecost · Mar Barthulmai Shleeha and Mar Barnabas · Foundation Day of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy
readings: Justified by faith, we have peace with God; God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit
“We will come to them and make our home with them”
2027-06-11.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Third Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers Mar Barthulmai Shleeha (St Bartholomew the Apostle) and Mar Barnabas, and keeps the Foundation Day of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy: on 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI, by the bull Christo Pastorum Principi, erected the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla.
2027-06-11.verse: Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.
theo: Today is a family feast for our Church. On 11 June 1932, Pope Pius XI, by the apostolic constitution Christo Pastorum Principi, erected the hierarchy of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church, with the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram under Archbishop Mar Ivanios and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla under Bishop Mar Theophilos. Less than two years earlier, on 20 September 1930 at Kollam, these two bishops and a small band of companions had made their profession of the Catholic faith and entered full communion with the Bishop of Rome, keeping the venerable West Syriac liturgy of their fathers. They left churches and properties behind; they brought with them the Holy Qurbono, the prayers of Mar Aprem and the faith of the Apostle Thomas. In 1932 the Church gave that small flock a home of its own: bishops, sees, a hierarchy, an ordered life within the one Catholic communion. In 2005 our Church was raised to the rank of a Major Archiepiscopal Church. We thank God today for all of it, and we remember with respect our brothers and sisters of the Malankara Orthodox and Jacobite Churches, with whom we share the same roots, the same liturgy and the same fathers, praying together for the unity that Christ desires.

The readings the Panchangam gives for this day could hardly be more fitting. St Paul writes: “Therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have obtained access to this grace in which we stand.” Access and standing: the language of someone who has been brought into a house and given a place in it. And the source of it all is not human planning but divine love: “hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.” St Augustine loved this verse above almost any other; he taught that the very love with which we love God is itself God's gift, poured out by the Spirit, so that whatever good we do is grace from beginning to end (On the Spirit and the Letter 5, in substance). Paul goes on to speak of reconciliation: “For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more surely, having been reconciled, will we be saved by his life.” The reunion of 1930 was a work of reconciliation, and Mar Ivanios understood it not as a victory over anyone but as a step towards the unity for which Christ prayed. The work is not finished. Every Christian division is a wound in the body of Christ, and the love poured into our hearts asks us to keep praying, to keep speaking kindly, and to keep the door open.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks at the Last Supper of the home that God makes with those who love him: “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.” Before this he has promised: “I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you,” and he has spoken of “another Advocate, to be with you forever.” A hierarchy is not, in the first place, an organisation chart. It is one of the ways the Lord keeps that promise: through bishops in communion with the successor of Peter, through the sacraments they celebrate and the faith they guard, the Holy Spirit makes sure that the flock is never left orphaned. St Gregory the Great, preaching on this Gospel, said that the proof of love is the display of works: we show that we love by keeping his word (Homilies on the Gospels 30, in substance). Our Church will celebrate this anniversary well, not with speeches only, but by being a home where the Father and the Son are glad to live: faithful to the word, generous to the poor, eager for unity, joyful in the liturgy.

The Panchangam also remembers two apostles today. Mar Barthulmai, St Bartholomew, is one of the Twelve whose names stand in every list of the apostles; many in the tradition identify him with Nathanael, of whom Jesus said: “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!” An ancient report preserved by Eusebius says that when the teacher Pantaenus travelled to India, he found Christians there who had a Gospel of Matthew left to them by Bartholomew (Church History 5.10); the tradition of the Churches places his martyrdom in Armenia. Mar Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, was called by the apostles “son of encouragement”. He sold his field for the poor, he took the newly converted Saul by the hand when everyone else was afraid of him, and he was sent to Antioch, where “the disciples were first called Christians”. It was in that church of Antioch, while they were worshipping the Lord and fasting, that the Holy Spirit said: “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” Our liturgy comes to us from the Syriac tradition of Antioch, and next Wednesday we begin the Apostles' Fast. On this day of our Church, Barnabas teaches us to encourage, Bartholomew teaches us to be without deceit, and both teach us that a Church is built on the faith of the apostles.
outline: Ask: do I treat my Church as an institution I belong to, or as a home where God lives with us?
The reunion at Kollam and the erection of the hierarchy: a home given to a small flock.
Justified by faith, reconciled through the Son, filled with the love the Spirit pours out.
Bishops in communion with Peter's successor as one way the Lord keeps his promise to make his home with us.
The apostle without deceit and the son of encouragement; Antioch, prayer and fasting.
“We will come to them and make our home with them.”
live: Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and our eparchies, and for one family in your parish that has drifted away.
Speak one word of encouragement this week to someone who is new, struggling or doubted by others.
2027-06-11.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you promised not to leave us orphaned, and in your love you gave our Syro-Malankara Church a home within the one Catholic communion. We thank you for Mar Ivanios, Mar Theophilos and all who walked with them, for the hierarchy erected in 1932, and for all our bishops, priests, religious and faithful. Pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, keep us faithful to your word, and make our Church a home where the Father and you are glad to dwell. Through the prayers of Mar Barthulmai, your apostle without deceit, and of Mar Barnabas, son of encouragement, heal the divisions among your disciples and bring all who call on your name into the unity you desire. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono celebrated by our bishops and priests in communion with the successor of Peter is the heart of the home the Lord has given us: around one altar the Father and the Son come to make their home with those who love them.
conn: Romans 5:1–11 speaks of peace, access and reconciliation; John 14:15–24 of the home God makes with those who love him. On the anniversary of 11 June 1932 both describe what the Church received: an ordered home in the one Catholic communion.

Acts 11:22–26 tells how Barnabas was sent to Antioch, brought Saul there, and how the disciples were first called Christians there; Acts 13:1–3 shows the church of Antioch worshipping and fasting when the Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul. Our Church's liturgy belongs to the Syriac tradition of Antioch, and the Apostles' Fast begins next Wednesday (16 June).
Bartholomew is named in every list of the Twelve (Matthew 10:3; Acts 1:13); many in the tradition identify him with Nathanael of John 1:45–49, the Israelite in whom there is no deceit.
fathers: The love of God poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit (Romans 5:5) is not the love by which God loves us only, but the love by which he makes us lovers of him: even our loving is his gift (On the Spirit and the Letter 5 and 32, in substance).
The proof of love is the display of works: whoever says that he loves God and does not keep his word is deceived (Homilies on the Gospels 30, on John 14:23, in substance).

When Pantaenus went as far as India, he found that the Gospel of Matthew had come there before him, left by the apostle Bartholomew (Church History 5.10, in substance; the India of ancient writers may mean lands beyond Arabia).
magis: The individual Churches, whether of the East or of the West, are of equal dignity; none is superior to the others by reason of its rite, and all enjoy the same rights and obligations under the guidance of the Roman Pontiff (in substance).
The particular Churches are formed in the image of the universal Church; in and from them the one and only Catholic Church comes into being.
The Church must breathe with her two lungs, the East and the West, and the treasures of the Eastern traditions belong to the whole Church (in substance).

2027-06-11.question: Do I love my Church as a home given by God, and do I help to make it one for others?

family.explain: Today is a birthday for our Church. In 1932 the Pope gave our Malankara Catholic Church its own bishops and its own dioceses, so that our people would have a home in the big family of the Catholic Church. Jesus says that he and the Father come to live in the hearts of those who love him. We also remember two apostles: Bartholomew, whom Jesus praised as a man without lies, and Barnabas, whose name means son of encouragement.
family.intention: We pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and our priests, and for the unity of all Christians in Kerala and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be a Barnabas this week and encourage someone?”

illus: An old man in a parish near Thiruvalla used to tell his grandchildren how his own grandfather had joined the Catholic communion in the early 1930s. The family had to leave the church where they had been baptised and married, and for some years they worshipped in a thatched shed with a mud floor. When the rain came through the roof during the Qurbono, the men held umbrellas over the altar. The old man would say: we had nothing, but my grandfather used to tell us that when we heard the bishop was coming to us as our own shepherd, it was as if we had been given a house. Then he would add, more quietly: and we must never speak unkindly of the family we came from. They are still our brothers.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you do not leave us orphaned. Pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, make our Church a home where you dwell, and make us encouragers like Barnabas. Amen.
share: Since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). Where do I need God's peace today?
I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you (John 14:18). When has the Church been a home to me?
Barnabas (which means “son of encouragement”) (Acts 4:36). Whom can I encourage this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make your home with us.
interc: For the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church on the anniversary of her hierarchy: for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops, priests, religious and faithful.
For the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla, and for all our eparchies and missions in India and abroad.
For the unity of all Christians, especially for our brothers and sisters of the Malankara Orthodox and Jacobite Churches, with whom we share one heritage.
For all who are discouraged, newly converted or doubted by others, that they may meet a Barnabas.
For the Church in Armenia, Cyprus and the Middle East, lands of the apostles Bartholomew and Barnabas.
pm.close: Father, you reconciled us to yourself through the death of your Son and you pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. On this day of our Church, keep us in the unity of the one Catholic communion, make us one with all who love your Son, and let us be a home where you are glad to dwell. Through the prayers of Mar Barthulmai and Mar Barnabas, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The hierarchy of a Church is its ordered structure of bishops in their sees, in communion with the Bishop of Rome. In the Eastern Catholic Churches a diocese is called an eparchy and its bishop an eparch; an archeparchy is the see of a metropolitan archbishop. On 11 June 1932 the Syro-Malankara hierarchy began with one archeparchy (Thiruvananthapuram) and one eparchy (Tiruvalla).
kidsaint: Barnabas, the friend who stood up

When Saul stopped persecuting Christians and became a follower of Jesus, the disciples in Jerusalem were afraid of him. They did not believe he had really changed. Only one man was brave enough to take Saul by the hand: Barnabas. He brought Saul to the apostles and told them how Jesus had spoken to him on the road. Because Barnabas stood up for him, Saul became the great St Paul. Barnabas's name means son of encouragement. Lesson: be the one who stands up for a new or lonely friend.

homily: Dear friends, today is a family feast for our Church. On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI erected the hierarchy of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church, with the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla. Two years before, in 1930, Mar Ivanios, Mar Theophilos and a few companions had entered full communion with the Catholic Church, leaving buildings and properties behind, but keeping our beautiful liturgy and the faith of our fathers.

St Paul tells us today: since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). And he tells us the source of it all: God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us (Romans 5:5). Our Church was born from that love, and from a longing for reconciliation and unity.

In the Gospel Jesus promises: I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you (John 14:18). And again: we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23). Through our bishops in communion with the successor of Peter, through the sacraments and through the faith they guard, the Lord keeps that promise. Our Church is meant to be a home where God lives and where every one of us belongs.

Today the Panchangam also remembers two apostles. Mar Barthulmai, Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, whom many identify with Nathanael, the Israelite in whom there is no deceit. And Mar Barnabas, son of encouragement, who stood by Saul when others were afraid, and who was set apart by the Holy Spirit at Antioch while the church was praying and fasting.

So on this day let us thank God for our Church, pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our bishops, and pray for the unity of all Christians, especially our brothers and sisters of the other Malankara Churches. And let us be like Barnabas: people who encourage, who open the door, who make the Church a home. Amen.
kids: Children, today is like a birthday for our Malankara Catholic Church! In 1932 the Pope gave our Church its own bishops and its own dioceses, so that we would have a home in the big family of the Catholic Church. Jesus said: I will not leave you alone like orphans. We also remember two friends of Jesus: Bartholomew, who never told lies, and Barnabas, who always encouraged people. When a new child comes to your class or your Sunday school, be a Barnabas: smile, sit with them and help them feel at home.

concl: On 11 June 1932 the Lord kept his promise not to leave his flock orphaned and gave our Church a home within the one Catholic communion.
The love poured into our hearts by the Spirit makes us reconcilers, honest like Bartholomew and encouragers like Barnabas.
